summary.en: Israel has expanded its presence in southern Lebanon by building new road networks and opening bases, while continuing strikes on Qantara, overflights that wounded a Lebanese footballer and the detention of a 65‑year-old retired engineer. Hezbollah has arrested five members in Batroun, maintained artillery fire on Israeli positions and begun cash payments to war victims and displaced families. Former Iraqi MP Ahmed al-Alwani was found dead in Beirut, prompting a probe by France into alleged Israeli war crimes. UN peacekeepers are preparing to exit Lebanon as displaced families face devastation, and Israel’s actions are disrupting ecosystems, including Lebanon’s wheat crop. 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel har utvidet sin tilstedeværelse i sørlige Libanon ved å bygge nye veinett og åpne baser, samtidig som de fortsetter angrep på Qantara, overflyvninger som såret en libanesisk fotballspiller og fengslingen av en 65‑år gammel pensjonert ingeniør. Hezbollah har arrestert fem medlemmer i Batroun, opprettholdt artilleribrann mot israelske posisjoner og innført kontantutbetalinger til krigsofre og fordrevne familier. Den tidligere irakiske MP Ahmed al-Alwani ble funnet død i Beirut, noe som førte til en etterforskning fra Frankrike av påståtte israelske krigsforbrytelser. FN-fredsbevarere forbereder seg på å forlate Libanon mens fordrevne familier står overfor ødeleggelse, og Israels handlinger forstyrrer økosystemer, inkludert Libanons hveteavling. 4 335 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
